Part 2&3 人物 PEOPLE

Describe a person who makes plans a lot and is good at planning

描述一个总做计划且擅长规划的人

⚠️ AI 范例，仅供学习 — IELTS 口语全程独立完成，背诵照搬 AI 答案会被考官识别为背稿。

Part 2 话题卡片

Describe a person who makes plans a lot and is good at planning

  • Who he/she is (他/她是谁)
  • How you knew him/her (你是怎么认识他/她的)
  • What plans he/she makes (他/她做什么计划)
  • And explain how you feel about this person (并解释你对这个人的感受)

问题与答案

Cue CardDescribe a person who makes plans a lot and is good at planning

I'd like to talk about my girlfriend, who is probably the most organised person I've ever met. She's a university student like me, and we've been together for about two years now. As for how I knew her, we actually met in the same class during our first year of university. We sat next to each other, started chatting about assignments, and eventually became close. It didn't take long for me to notice how disciplined she was with her studies. In terms of what plans she makes, she plans almost everything. She keeps a detailed study schedule, breaking each semester into weekly goals, and she always knows exactly what she needs to finish each day. Before exams, she maps out a revision timetable weeks in advance, and she even plans her weekends, balancing study with rest. Thanks to that habit, she's won scholarships two years in a row, which I think says a lot about her. The reason I admire her so much is that her planning isn't rigid or stressful, it actually gives her freedom. Because she knows what needs to be done, she never panics at the last minute, and she still finds time to relax. Watching her, I've learned that good planning isn't about controlling every minute, it's about staying calm and in control. Honestly, she's inspired me to be more organised myself, and I'm grateful to have her as a role model.

讲的是我女朋友，她是我见过最有条理的人。我们大一同班认识的，坐邻座聊作业慢慢熟起来。她几乎什么都做计划：把每学期拆成每周目标，每天该完成什么清清楚楚；考前几周就排好复习表，连周末都规划好学习和休息。靠这个习惯她连续两年拿奖学金。我佩服她是因为她的计划不僵化也不累人，反而给她自由，从不临时慌乱，还有时间放松。她让我学会有条理，我很感激有她这个榜样。

Q2Do you think it's important to plan ahead?

Yes, I think it's very important, though the level of detail can vary. Planning ahead helps people use their time efficiently and reduces stress, because you always know what's coming next. It also makes goals more achievable, since a big task becomes manageable when it's broken into smaller steps. That said, I don't think every minute needs to be planned, since being too rigid can make life feel mechanical. So the key is to plan enough to stay organised, but stay flexible.

非常重要，但详细程度可以不同。提前计划能高效利用时间、减少压力，因为你知道接下来要做什么；把大任务拆成小步骤也更容易达成。但不必每分钟都规划，太死板会让生活变得机械。关键是计划到有条理，同时保持灵活。

Q3What activities do we need to plan ahead?

I'd say anything that involves limited resources or high stakes. For example, travel definitely needs planning, since you have to book transport and accommodation in advance. Big purchases, like buying a house or a car, also require long-term financial planning. On top of that, career and education decisions need careful thought, because they shape your future for years. Even everyday things, like cooking for a family, benefit from a bit of planning. So basically, the more costly or complex the activity, the more planning it needs.

凡是涉及有限资源或高风险的事都需要计划。比如旅行必须提前订交通和住宿；买房买车这类大额消费需要长期财务规划；职业和教育决定影响未来很多年，更要慎重考虑；就连给家人做饭这类日常事，有点计划也更好。总之越花钱越复杂的事越需要计划。

Q4Do you think children should plan their future careers?

I think it's good for children to have a general sense of direction, but not to be locked into a specific career too early. At a young age, interests change quickly, so a rigid plan could limit their exploration. That said, exposing them to different fields and helping them understand their strengths is valuable, since it gives them a starting point. I'd say the ideal approach is to encourage curiosity and let the plan develop gradually, rather than forcing a decision in childhood.

孩子应该有大方向，但不宜过早锁定具体职业。小时候兴趣变得快，死板的计划会限制探索。不过让他们接触不同领域、了解自己的长处很有价值，能给他们一个起点。理想做法是鼓励好奇心，让计划慢慢成形，而不是小时候就逼着做决定。

Q5Should children ask their teachers or parents for advice when making plans?

Yes, I think they should, because adults have experience that children simply don't have yet. Teachers understand a child's academic strengths and can suggest suitable directions, while parents know their child's personality and can offer practical guidance. That said, the final decision should still be the child's, since a plan only works if the person actually wants to follow it. So adults should act as advisors, not decision-makers, and children should learn to weigh advice against their own interests.

应该问，因为大人有孩子没有的经验。老师了解孩子的学业强项，能建议合适的方向；父母了解孩子的性格，能给出实际指导。但最终决定权还是应该在孩子手里，因为计划只有本人愿意执行才有效。大人应该当顾问而不是决策者，孩子要学会权衡建议和自己的兴趣。

Q6Is making study plans popular among young people?

Yes, I'd say it's quite popular these days, especially among students. With so much competition, many young people feel they need to organise their time carefully to keep up, so study plans have become a common habit. Apps and online tools have also made planning easier, which encourages more people to try it. That said, I think many plans are made but not strictly followed, since young people often get distracted. So it's popular in theory, but sticking to the plan is the real challenge.

现在挺流行的，尤其学生。竞争激烈，很多年轻人觉得必须好好安排时间才能跟上，做学习计划成了常见习惯；各种 App 和在线工具也让规划更容易。但我觉得很多人是做了计划却没严格执行，年轻人容易分心。所以理论上流行，坚持执行才是真正的挑战。

Q7待补充

Yes, I think it's an excellent hobby for elderly people. For one thing, it gives them gentle daily exercise and a reason to move around, which is good for their health. It also provides a sense of purpose and routine after retirement, which can prevent loneliness and boredom. On top of that, watching plants grow is genuinely rewarding, and it gives them something to share with their families. So I'd say it's one of the most beneficial hobbies for older people.

对老人来说是非常好的爱好：每天有轻量的活动量，对身体好；退休后有了寄托和规律，能避免孤独无聊；看着植物长大很有成就感，还能和家人分享。可以说是最适合老人的爱好之一。
